page: Amazon Web Services inf1.24xlarge is an accelerated computing instance engineered for machine learning inference and built upon the Nitro system. The server integrates 16 custom AWS Inferentia chips providing a combined 128 GB of accelerator memory alongside an x86_64 host system. Compute capacity is driven by 96 vCPUs across 48 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor operating at 2.5 GHz, supported by 192 GB of DDR4 system memory clocked at 3 GHz. The instance delivers a 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and persistent storage must be provisioned externally as no local disk storage is included.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-core processing and host memory throughput. Multi-threaded CPU metrics place the instance in the top 25%, achieving a stress-ng score of 94,571.8 and a PassMark CPU score of 62,408.52, while single-core performance remains average. Uncached memory reads reach 232.48 GB/s, and Redis operations exceed 79.6 million operations per second. Conversely, autoregressive text generation under large language models registers in the bottom 10% across test categories, showing 40.73 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model and 5.46 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model.

The inf1.24xlarge delivers dense hardware resources suited for high-concurrency inference tasks compiled for AWS Inferentia architecture. Because internal storage is absent, data pipelines depend entirely on network-attached volumes. The instance fits high-throughput deep learning inference workloads such as computer vision, speech synthesis, recommendation engines, and standard encoder-based NLP models, but exhibits clear architectural tradeoffs when handling modern autoregressive text generation.
description: Amazon Web Services inf1.24xlarge is an accelerated computing instance designed for machine learning inference. Powered by the Nitro hypervisor, it features 16 AWS Inferentia chips with 128 GB of accelerator memory paired with 96 vCPUs on an Intel Xeon 8275CL processor (48 physical cores at 2.5 GHz). The system contains 192 GB of DDR4 system memory and delivers 100 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, with zero local storage provided. Host performance demonstrates strong multi-core computation and memory bandwidth, reaching 94,571.8 on stress-ng multi-core tests and 232.48 GB/s on large uncached memory reads. While well-equipped with network and processing scale, benchmark evaluations show sluggish autoregressive text generation on larger language models. Consequently, the inf1.24xlarge is best matched with classical deep learning inference pipelines, computer vision, recommendation models, and high-throughput network-dependent processing workflows that leverage custom AWS Neuron compiler optimizations.
